prompt.value: Consider the following relations defined on the set of integers: 𝑅1 = {(𝑥, 𝑦): 𝑥, 𝑦 ∈ 𝑍 and ∣𝑥 − 𝑦∣ ≤ 3} and 𝑅2 = {(𝑥, 𝑦): 𝑥, 𝑦 ∈ 𝑍 and 3 divides 𝑥 − 𝑦}. Choose the correct option(s).

options.value: 𝑅2 is symmetric but not transitive.
𝑅1 is an equivalence relation but 𝑅2 is not an equivalence relation.
𝑅2 is an equivalence relation but 𝑅1 is not an equivalence relation.

explanation.value: 𝑅1: ∣𝑥 − 𝑥∣ = 0 ≤ 3 (reflexive) and symmetric, but not transitive (e.g. ∣0 − 3∣ ≤ 3, ∣3 − 6∣ ≤ 3 but ∣0 − 6∣ = 6 > 3), so it is NOT an equivalence relation. 𝑅2 (congruence mod 3) is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation. So option 0 (R1 reflexive & symmetric) and option 3 (R2 equivalence, R1 not) are correct; option 1 is wrong (R2 IS transitive); option 2 is wrong (it is the reverse).

prompt.value: Let 𝑓(𝑥) = ∣𝑥2 + 1∣ − 1. Which of the following option(s) are true for 𝑓?

options.value: 𝑓 is defined for all 𝑥 ∈ 𝑅.
The minimum value of 𝑓 is 0.

explanation.value: Since 𝑥2 + 1 > 0 for all 𝑥, ∣𝑥2 + 1∣ = 𝑥2 + 1, so 𝑓(𝑥) = 𝑥2. It is defined for all real 𝑥 (option 0 true). It is not one-one since 𝑓( − 𝑎) = 𝑓(𝑎) (option 1 false). Range is [0, ∞), not ( − ∞, 0) (option 2 false). Minimum value is 𝑓(0) = 0 (option 3 true).

prompt.value: Consider two polynomials 𝑝(𝑥) = − 𝑥5 + 5𝑥4 − 7𝑥 − 2 and 𝑞(𝑥) = − 𝑥5 + 5𝑥4 − 𝑥2 − 2. Which of the following options is/are true?

options.value: 𝑝(𝑥) has at most 4 turning points.
The quotient obtained while dividing 𝑞(𝑥) by 𝑝(𝑥) is a constant.

explanation.value: Leading term of 𝑝 is −𝑥5, so as 𝑥 → + ∞, 𝑝(𝑥) → − ∞ (option 1 true, option 0 false). A degree-5 polynomial has at most 5 − 1 = 4 turning points (option 2 true). Both have the same leading term, and 𝑞(𝑥) − 𝑝(𝑥) = − 𝑥2 + 7𝑥 has degree < 5, so 𝑞 = 1 ⋅ 𝑝 + ( − 𝑥2 + 7𝑥), giving a constant quotient 1 (option 3 true).
